cases.prompt: A modal can be: closed; open with form fields being edited; submitting (a request in flight); or showing a server error. Model this as a TypeScript type so each variant carries only the data it needs and callers can switch exhaustively. Today the code has one interface with four mutually-exclusive optional fields plus a string 'phase'. Give me the type and the consumer switch.

I have a config object with themes = ['light', 'dark', 'system'] and defaultPref = 'system'. I want a readonly literal-union of valid theme names so autocomplete works and defaults are type-checked, without retyping the list or using a cast. How do I type this so TypeScript derives the exact literal values from the value itself?

We pass user ids and session ids around and keep mixing them up; both are plain strings. Give me a technique that makes passing a user id where a session id is expected a compile error, with no runtime overhead.

An endpoint returns either { ok: true, data: T } or { ok: false, error: { code, message } }. Handlers currently do `(await res.json()) as any`. Type the response shape and show how a caller narrows on ok to get the data or the typed error, without unsafe casts.
I have a getSetting(name) backed by a map. Callers treat a missing setting inconsistently: some expect null, some crash. Pick one contract, justify it, and show the signature.
A fetch inside loadProfile fails with a low-level ECONNRESET. Wrap it so the new error tells an operator which profile/task failed and still keeps the original error reachable for debugging.
A background job sends an email and retries on failure. It must not retry a 4xx bad-request, but should retry transient network/5xx with backoff. Sketch the failure taxonomy and the retry decision.
Several steps in sequence (validate, auth, save) each can fail with distinct causes. I don't want try/catch pyramids and the caller needs to know which step failed. Pick a shape.
Typeahead search fires a request per keystroke, and responses can arrive out of order. Write the handler so only the latest query's result is applied, and wire cancellation.
We must POST 1000 rows to an API that tolerates about 10 concurrent requests. Promise.all-ing all 1000 overwhelms it. Give a pattern that runs them with a small concurrency limit.
A click handler kicks off a background save and returns immediately; it calls saveThing() without awaiting and sometimes throws 'Unhandled rejection'. Fix the ownership.
A slow partner API can hang. Wrap the call with a timeout so we fail fast, and make sure the timed-out branch cleans up (doesn't leak the in-flight request or swallow its later rejection).
